finding: §4.1.7 requires that `On each successful `cr map record`, `cr` MUST derive `intent-gaps.ndjson` mechanically as the claims of the current round mapped to zero units.` That derivation is a pure function of claims and mapping and has no place for `set_aside_note`, which §4.1.8 stamps onto a gap entry (`MUST stamp `set_aside_note` on that gap entry after checking the note exists`) and which §4.1.3 lists as an entry field. So any later `cr map record` — the ordinary way to add one more mapping — rewrites the file and destroys every set-aside already recorded, and §10.2.3's block (`MUST block completeness until it is either mapped, or set aside through `cr claims set-aside``) silently returns for claims the agent already judged out of scope. §4.1.8 calls that judgement `the agent's call, never `cr`'s`, yet §4.1.7 revokes it mechanically and reports nothing.
suggestion: Add to §4.1.7: the derivation MUST carry forward `set_aside_note` for any claim whose entry already held one.

finding: §5.3.2's derivation admits an add-only first hunk: `the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line, or when that hunk only adds lines, its first pre-image line`. A pre-image line of an add-only hunk is a line the patch never changed, and the agent chooses it by choosing where to insert. That reopens the steering the repair was meant to close, in two ways. An inert insertion (dead code, an unreachable statement) breaks nothing, so `no-test-failed` is guaranteed by construction, yet §6.2.2 accepts the probe for any record whose anchor contains that agent-placed line and §8.1.7 renders `kind`, `target`, and `result` to the author as the strongest register they can check — a mutation probe reporting an untested line that may be well tested. And because only the first hunk feeds the derivation, an agent can lead with an add-only hunk to place `target` wherever it likes while a later hunk performs the real mutation elsewhere, so a genuine `no-test-failed` is attributed to a line the mutation never touched. §5.3's own framing, `proves a test gap by breaking production code`, does not hold for a patch that removes nothing.
suggestion: Delete the add-only branch and reject the input instead: in §5.3.2, `cr` MUST reject with exit code 1 a mutation patch whose first hunk removes or replaces no line, since an addition breaks nothing at `target`.

finding: The repaired derivation is still multi-valued in two shapes I must test. (a) Ordering: 'the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line' never says what orders hunks. §5.3.1 says 'The agent supplies a mutation as a unified diff', so a two-file patch may list b/z.go before b/a.go; one implementation takes the first hunk in patch-text order, another the first hunk in ascending path order, and they derive different paths. (b) The add-only branch: 'or when that hunk only adds lines, its first pre-image line'. For `@@ -39,7 +39,8 @@` with three context lines before a single inserted line, 'the hunk's first pre-image line' is 39 and 'the pre-image line at the insertion point' is 41; for a `-U0` patch `@@ -41,0 +42 @@` the hunk has no pre-image line at all and the clause names nothing. This is not cosmetic: §6.2.2 supports a record 'only when its `target` falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path', which for a single-line anchor is one line, so the choice decides between a `probed` grade and rejection with exit code 1 — and inserting an early return is one of the commonest mutations, so the add-only branch is the common path, not the edge.
suggestion: In §5.3.2 pin both: 'the first hunk in patch order' and, for an add-only hunk, 'the pre-image line its first added line follows'.

finding: Round 11's repair to §5.4.4 made a gap probe support a finding only when `its baseline passed per §5.2.5 **and** the finding's `claim` field names a claim mapped to the finding's unit`. §4.6.6 says that when the intent axis is unavailable per §4.5.3, `the mapping MUST be treated as empty`. An empty mapping maps no claim to any unit, so the second conjunct is unsatisfiable and no gap probe can ever support a finding in that configuration — even though §4.5.2 disables the test axis only when the profile declares no `tests.cmd`, keeping the two axes independent, and §3.2 explicitly supports a PR with no resolvable issue key (`cr` MUST continue with an empty intent and mark the intent axis unavailable). The whole `probed` path of §5.4 dies silently: the agent keeps spending the §5.6.4 budget on probes that can never grade, §5.4.4's `Severity MUST be at least `high`` can never fire, and nothing discloses it, while §4.5.4 requires every lens that did not run to be stated with its reason. §5.3's mutation probe carries no such coupling, so the two probe kinds behave incomparably on the same repository.
suggestion: Add to §5.4.4: when the intent axis is unavailable per §4.5.3 the claim condition MUST NOT apply, and the baseline condition alone governs.

finding: The repair made §5.4.4's support test mechanical but no longer restrictive: `only when its baseline passed per §5.2.5 and the finding's claim field names a claim mapped to the finding's unit`. §4.1.1 maps units to claims as a matter of course, so on any mapped unit the second conjunct is satisfied by writing the unit's own claim id into `claim` — a field the agent writes. The remaining tie between experiment and finding is §6.2.2's target-in-anchor test, and for `kind: gap` §5.5 makes `target` the agent's `--target`, validated only to exist at head; the anchor is agent-written too. So an agent that supplies any test which fails for any reason can attach `probed` to any finding on a mapped unit, on a probe §5.4.4 itself says cr cannot read: `either the behaviour is wrong or the supplied test is wrong, and cr cannot distinguish the two`. Nothing in the chain establishes that the failing test exercises the finding, and `probed` is the register §8.1.7 presents as the one the author need not take on trust.
suggestion: Mirror §5.4.5 and remove the branch rather than qualifying it: in §5.4.4, a `failed` gap probe MUST NOT support a `probed` grade — it is recorded and offered as a reproduction, leaving the record `argued` and therefore a question under §6.3, with severity at most `medium`.

finding: Repair 2 relocated round 11's forgery rather than closing it. The row now reads "| `axis` | computed | The axis of the record's `role`, written by `cr` |", so §6.1.4's "any other field marked computed" does reject an agent-written `axis` — but the field it is now derived from is still agent-written and entirely unvalidated: "| `role` | yes | The role that produced it |". No clause anywhere binds a record's `role` to the role that actually produced it, or even requires it to resolve; the only such check in the spec is for cells (§4.5.6: "reject with exit code 1 a cell naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role"), and §6.1.3 and §6.5.1 impose no counterpart on a record. A role on the `test` axis can therefore write `role: correctness` in its own §4.6.2 output file, `cr` computes `axis: correctness`, and §6.2's cited row — "and the record's `axis` is not `test`" — is satisfied, restoring exactly the assertion register that repair 2 was applied to remove. The derivation also has no defined behaviour when `role` does not resolve at all, which §6.2 now needs before it can grade anything.
suggestion: Mirror repair 2 one field up, in the same table and with no new field or concept: change the `role` row to "| `role` | computed | The role whose §4.6.2 output file the record arrived in, written by `cr` |", so §6.1.4 rejects an agent-written `role` and `axis` derives from a value `cr` observed.

finding: Round 11's repair made `axis` computed — `| axis | computed | The axis of the record's role, written by cr |` — but it moved the write one field over rather than closing the path. §6.2.1 now names the grading inputs as `axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record; of those, `role` (which `axis` is derived from), `unit`, and `anchor` are agent-written, and nothing in §6.1, §6.3, or §6.5 validates them. Two unearned assertions follow. (a) §6.2's `cited` row bars the test axis — `and the record's axis is not test` — which is the bar §4.4.2 exists to enforce; a test-adequacy record that writes `role: correctness` computes `axis: correctness`, and one citation outside its unit grades it `cited`, so a test-coverage claim reaches the assertion register with no probe. §6.1.4 rejects a supplied `axis` but is silent on `role`, and §6.1.3 checks only that required fields are present, never that `role` is the role that produced the file per §4.6.2. (b) `unit` is the boundary in `lies outside the record's own unit`, and the agent picks it: naming any other unit makes a citation into the record's own diff count as outside, so the record cites itself into `cited`. §6.2.1's closing sentence — `No field the agent writes can move a location across the boundary` — is therefore false as written.
suggestion: Add one validation clause to §6.1: `cr merge` MUST reject with exit code 1 a record whose `role` is not the role whose prompt named its input file per §4.6.2, and `cr merge` and `cr record` MUST reject a record whose `anchor.path` is not among the named `unit`'s file paths.

finding: Round 11's repair moved `axis` from agent-written to `| `axis` | computed | The axis of the record's `role`, written by `cr` |`, but it only moved the forgery one field up. `role` is still `| `role` | yes | The role that produced it |` — agent-written, and no section validates it. §4.5.6 rejects a cell `naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role`, and §6.1.3/§6.1.4 reject only missing-required and computed fields; nothing rejects a record whose `role` names an unknown or inactive role. Since §6.2's `cited` row turns on `the record's `axis` is not `test``, a test-adequacy record written with `role: correctness` is computed to `axis: correctness` and can be graded `cited` off a citation to a test file — precisely what §4.4.2 forbids (`Citations to test files MUST NOT grade it `cited``). The guard §4.4.2 states is therefore unenforceable, and a test-adequacy record can assert rather than ask.
suggestion: In §6.1.3 add: `cr merge` and `cr record` MUST also reject with exit code 1 a record whose `role` does not name a role active for the current round per §4.5.1, naming the line and the role id. The resolved role corpus is already required at merge by §6.5.1.

finding: §6.2.1 closes the grade inputs: "The only inputs are `axis`, `unit`, `anchor`, `citations`, and the referenced probe record". §5.4.4 conditions a gap probe's support on "the finding's `claim` field names a claim mapped to the finding's unit". `claim` is not in that list and `mapping.ndjson` is not an input at all, so `probed` for a gap-probe record cannot be computed from the enumerated inputs. The two clauses contradict each other and I would have to pick one — either read a field §6.2.1 forbids, or ignore the support condition §5.4.4 mandates.
suggestion: Extend §6.2.1's list to "`axis`, `unit`, `claim`, `anchor`, `citations`, the current round's mapping, and the referenced probe record".

finding: §4.1.7 requires that "On each successful `cr map record`, `cr` MUST derive `intent-gaps.ndjson` mechanically as the claims of the current round mapped to zero units", while §4.1.8 stamps `set_aside_note` on a gap entry. A second `cr map record` in the same round re-derives the file mechanically, so a claim still mapped to zero units gets a fresh entry with no `set_aside_note`, and §10.2.3 re-blocks completeness on a claim the human already set aside. Nothing says the stamp survives re-derivation, so I would have to invent the preservation rule.
suggestion: Add to §4.1.7: re-derivation MUST carry forward `set_aside_note` for a claim that still has an entry.

finding: §4.6.5 gates the remaining axes: "`cr review <pr>` MUST refuse the remaining axes with exit code 4 until a mapping exists for the current round and head". §4.1.6 has `cr map record` "replace `mapping.ndjson` for the current round with one `{claim, unit}` pair per line", and §3.3.1 and §9.3.4 clear that same file. A legitimate recording of zero pairs — every unit unmapped, the case §4.1.2 and §4.1.3 exist for — is byte-identical to never having recorded one, and no per-PR state in §2.3 distinguishes them, so the gate never opens.
suggestion: State in §4.1.6 that a successful `cr map record` marks the mapping recorded for the current round and head, and that §4.6.5's gate reads that mark rather than the file's contents.

finding: §5.1.6's cleanliness test requires `no leftover probe artefact exists — no file under any path matching `tests.probe_path_template` with its `<probe-id>` position replaced by `*``, and the clause is not restricted to untracked files even though the adjacent sentence shows the distinction was in view (`Other untracked files are ignored`). A probe artefact is untracked by construction, but the glob is evaluated against the whole worktree, and §2.4 leaves `tests.probe_path_template` user-configurable with only the constraint that `the result matches its own `tests.globs``. A template such as `tests/<probe-id>_test.go` globs to `tests/*_test.go` and matches tracked test files, so every freshly created sandbox fails the check. §5.1.6 then requires that `A sandbox failing any of these checks MUST be recreated`, with no bound, and recreation reproduces the tracked file — an unbounded recreate loop that makes `cr test` and every probe unrunnable, reported each time per §11.1.
suggestion: In §5.1.6 restrict the artefact clause to untracked files: `no untracked file under any path matching `tests.probe_path_template`...`.

finding: §5.3.2 derives `target` as "the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line, or when that hunk only adds lines, its first pre-image line". A pure-insertion hunk written with no context (`@@ -42,0 +43,2 @@`) has an empty pre-image range, so "its first pre-image line" names nothing; written with context it names the hunk's first context line, which the mutation never touched. §6.2.2 requires `target` to fall inside the record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range, so the choice decides whether an insertion mutation can grade a finding at all.
suggestion: Replace the second branch with "or, when that hunk removes no line, the pre-image line its insertion follows, which is the hunk header's pre-image start".

finding: §5.4.4's repaired condition — the probe supports the finding only when its baseline passed 'and the finding's `claim` field names a claim mapped to the finding's unit' — cannot be satisfied from the axis that runs gap probes. Gap probes serve test adequacy, and nothing gives a `test` record a claim: §6.1 marks `claim` optional as 'The claim id, when the axis produces one', and §4.4 never mentions it. Worse, §4.6.6 says that when the intent axis is unavailable 'the mapping MUST be treated as empty', so on any PR whose issue key does not resolve per §3.2 the condition is false for every record and no gap probe can ever support a finding — leaving §4.4.2's 'A test-adequacy finding asserts only with an experiment' with no reachable experiment on that axis. I can write the negative test but not the positive one, because no clause says which findings carry `claim`.
suggestion: Make §5.4.4 read 'and, when the intent axis is active, the finding's `claim` names a claim mapped to its unit', and say in §4.4 that a gap-probed finding carries that claim.

finding: The new row '| `axis` | computed | The axis of the record's `role`, written by `cr` |' makes `axis` a function of `role`, and §6.2.1 names `axis` and `unit` as grading inputs, but no clause validates either reference. §4.5.6 rejects a cell 'naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role'; §6.1.3 rejects only records 'missing any field marked required'. So for a record whose `role` is absent from the resolved corpus, `axis` is uncomputable, and for one whose `unit` names no unit of the round, §6.2.1's containment test ('`path` is one of that unit's file paths') has no domain. Two conforming implementations: one rejects with exit code 1; the other leaves `axis` unset, which satisfies the `cited` row's 'the record's `axis` is not `test`' and grades the record `cited`. I cannot write either assertion.
suggestion: Extend §6.1.3: `cr merge` and `cr record` MUST also reject with exit code 1 a record whose `role` is not an active role or whose `unit` is not a unit of the current round.

finding: §6.1's row is "| `axis` | computed | The axis of the record's `role`, written by `cr` |", but `role` is agent-written and no clause requires it to name a role that exists after §2.5.4 resolution. For a record whose `role` does not resolve, `axis` has no value, §6.2's `cited` condition "the record's `axis` is not `test`" is undefined, and §6.4.2's "earliest role in corpus order per §2.5.5" has no position to order by. §4.5.6 rejects a cell "naming an unknown unit id or an inactive role"; there is no equivalent guard for a record, so I would have to invent one.
suggestion: Add to §6.1.3: a record whose `role` does not resolve to an active role MUST be rejected with exit code 1, naming the line and the role.

finding: §6.4.1 deduplicates 'by `(anchor.path, anchor.line, class)`', dropping `anchor.side` and `anchor.start_line`, while §7.4.1's waiver key includes the 'normalised hash of the anchored lines' and therefore does separate them. §6.1.2 resolves the two sides against different trees ('against the head for `side: RIGHT`, against the merge base for `side: LEFT`') and §3.4.4 partitions units by side, so a LEFT record about a deleted line and a RIGHT record about an added line collide at the same path and line number whenever LEFT and RIGHT numbering have drifted — the ordinary case in a file with a deletion before an addition. §6.4.2 may then elect the deletion record and §6.4.3 leaves the other in state `duplicate`, where §7.1 never drafts it. The assertion 'two records on opposite sides are not duplicates' contradicts the spec as written.
suggestion: Key §6.4.1 on `(anchor.path, anchor.side, anchor.start_line, anchor.line, class)`.

finding: §6.4.1 deduplicates by "(anchor.path, anchor.line, class)", omitting `anchor.side`. §9.2.1 admits both `RIGHT` and `LEFT` anchors, and §8.3.3 orders comments "then `side` (`LEFT` before `RIGHT`)" — a tiebreak that exists only because two comments can share `path`, `start_line`, and `line` and differ only by side. Under §6.4.1 those two records fall into one duplicate group and one is suppressed before it can ever reach the ordering §8.3.3 defines for it.
suggestion: Key §6.4.1 on `(anchor.path, anchor.side, anchor.line, class)`.

finding: §7.2's marker table says of `path`, `start_line`, `line`: "Re-validated per §6.1.2; aborts when the anchor no longer resolves". §9.2 requires the anchor to carry "a normalised content hash, and up to three lines of context on each side", and nothing says either is recomputed after such an edit. The stale hash is load-bearing: §7.4.1 keys a waiver on the "normalised hash of the anchored lines" and §9.3.6 keys the posted index identically, so a record whose lines were moved by hand is waived and indexed against code it no longer points at.
suggestion: Extend the row to "Re-validated per §6.1.2, and the anchor's content hash and context recomputed; aborts when the anchor no longer resolves".

finding: The third trigger, 'takes its grade from a citation with `origin: rule`', is not decidable from the record. §6.2's `cited` row is a disjunction — an entry qualifies when it 'either has `origin: rule` or lies outside the record's own unit' — so a record carrying one rule citation and one out-of-unit agent citation is `cited` under either entry alone. One implementation emits the provenance region whenever any citation carries `origin: rule`; another emits it only when the rule citation is the sole qualifier, which is what the trailing clause 'the last being the one that buys the assertion register mechanically' argues for. The two produce different posted bodies from the same record. The same sentence also leaves composition undefined when triggers coincide: 'The region names the machine origin, or the note and its source per §3.6.3, or the rule id with its `rationale`' gives no rule for a rule-generated suggestion sitting on a claim with `source: note`.
suggestion: In §8.1.6 replace the third trigger with 'carries any citation with `origin: rule`', and state that every applicable clause is named in the listed order.

finding: §9.3.3 makes `cr brief` `increment `meta.json`'s round index` and then §9.3.4 requires that `On that increment every record still in `draft` or `queued` MUST move to `stale``. Those records belong to the round that just ended, not the round now current. §9.3.5 forbids exactly that: `a command MUST read only the current round's records; earlier rounds are history`, and its exemption list is closed — `Waivers per §7.4, the context store per §3.6, and the posted index of §9.3.6 apply across rounds and are exempt from this scoping.` The staling of §9.3.4 is not among them, so an implementer following §9.3.5 leaves prior-round records permanently in `draft`/`queued`, the §9.1 transition row `draft`, `queued` | `stale` | `cr brief` on a new head never fires, and the `stale` state of §9.1 is unreachable.
suggestion: Add the §9.3.4 staling to §9.3.5's exemption list.

finding: §5.1.6 builds the leftover-artefact glob from `tests.probe_path_template` 'with its `<probe-id>` position replaced by `*`, which the template MUST contain exactly once', but no clause says what happens when a template contains it zero or twice. §2.4's sibling row for `tests.count_pattern` pins exactly this shape of failure — 'any other group count aborts with exit code 3 naming the profile' — so the convention exists and this row lacks it. Three conforming implementations: one aborts at profile load with exit code 3, one fails the §5.1.6 cleanliness check with exit code 4 at the first probe, one globs the literal template and never detects a leftover artefact at all.
suggestion: Append to §2.4's `tests.probe_path_template` row: a template not containing `<probe-id>` exactly once aborts with exit code 3 naming the profile.

finding: Repair 4's added branch is undefined for the input it was written for. The derivation now reads "the path and pre-image line of the first hunk's first removed or replaced line, or when that hunk only adds lines, its first pre-image line", but a hunk that only adds lines and carries no context has no pre-image line at all (`@@ -10,0 +11,3 @@`), so "its first pre-image line" names nothing. `target` is a grading input — §6.2.2 requires that "its `target` falls within that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range on the same path" — so an undefined target leaves the `probed` grade undefined for that patch.
suggestion: Narrow the branch to a line that always exists: replace "its first pre-image line" with "the pre-image line its insertion point follows".

finding: §8.2.1 requires that "A suggestion MUST map to a contiguous line range that exists in the PR diff on the `RIGHT` side" and §8.2.3 speaks of "the first replaced line", but no clause says which range a suggestion replaces; §6.1's `suggestion` is only "Exact replacement lines". The record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` is the only candidate, but it is nowhere stated, so §8.2.1, §8.2.2, and §8.2.3 each rest on a binding I would have to supply.
suggestion: Say in §8.2.1 that the range a suggestion replaces is the record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line`.

finding: §9.2 defines the anchor content hash as 'the normalised hash per §1.4 of the lines from `start_line` to `line` inclusive' and §6.2.2 tests containment over 'that record's `anchor.start_line`..`anchor.line` range', but nothing requires `start_line <= line`. §6.1.2 requires only 'an anchor that resolves', which speaks to existence, not ordering. For `start_line: 10, line: 4` the hash pre-image is undefined and the range is empty: one implementation rejects with exit code 1, another hashes the empty string, stores a §7.4.1 waiver key derived from it, and makes every probe unsupportable for that record.
suggestion: Add to §9.2: `start_line` MUST be less than or equal to `line`, and an anchor violating this MUST be rejected with exit code 1.
